newsitem.title: UKRAINE: FOCUS - Ukraine airline hails Austrian-Swiss deal.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Ukraine airline hails Austrian-Swiss deal.

text.p: Ukraine International Airlines (UIA), bolstered by an influx of cash from Swissair AG and Austrian Airlines, hopes to strengthen its position in the lucrative West European market.
"We have become part of an alliance. This will definitely improve our position and reputation in the world," UIA President Vitaly Potyemsky said in an interview late on Monday.
Swissair announced on Friday that it and Austrian Airlines had taken an 18.37 percent stake in UIA, investing $9.0 million.
Potyemsky said such alliances were the only way to survive growing competition.

"It's a great idea not to compete with each other but to cooperate. Austrian Airlines has worked out a scheme of survival for small carriers, which face tough competition with giants like British Airways or American Airlines and so on," he said.

Hundreds of small airlines which have sprung up across the former Soviet Union since it fell apart in 1991 are struggling to compete with each other and Western carriers, which generally offer more reliable and comfortable services.

But UIA, set up in 1992 as a Ukrainian-Irish venture, became profitable last year. It serves 12 West European cities with three leased Boeing 737s and Potyemsky said it planned to lease another Boeing early next year.
Swissair and AUA took their stake through UIA Beteiligungs GmbH, a Swissair-AUA joint venture set up for the purpose which is 22.22 percent owned by Swissair and 77.78 percent by AUA.

Potyemsky said the investment -- $2.0 million from Swissair and $7.0 million from AUA -- made perfect sense, allowing all three airlines to profit from UIA's knowledge of the Ukrainian market for foreign travel.
"Why, for example, should Austrian Airlines occupy Ukraine's domestic market -- it's more reasonable to buy a stake and then make profits from our successes inside Ukraine," he said.
UIA will be able to sell tickets through the Austrian and Swiss companies' offices around the world and the two airlines will each have a representative on UIA's board of directors.
Potyemsky said talks were underway with the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development for a $5 million credit.
Of UIA's total share capital is $49 million, the State Property Fund of Ukraine owns 68.37 percent and Guiness Peat Aviation of Ireland has 13.26 percent.

UIA made a profit of $1.5 million on sales of $47 million in the first nine months of 1996, up from $360,000 for the whole of last year when sales were $42 million. It expects to transport more than 180,000 passengers this year.
Among UIA's 12 West European routes are Zurich and Vienna.
Swissair serves the Zurich-Kiev route five times weekly in a codeshare agreement with UIA, while UIA operates a single weekly flight to Zurich on its own.

UIA is Ukraine's second biggest carrier. State-owned Air Ukraine inherited much of the fleet left by Soviet flag carrier Aeroflot and serves destinations in the former Soviet Union, eastern Europe, the Middle East, India, China and North America with ageing Soviet-built jets.
